$comment: The spec-to-ship pipeline. `shipConfig` is the whole of it: one block per track, and inside each the stages that track runs, written out in full. Nothing is inherited between tracks — what you read under a track is exactly what that track runs. Validate any edit with `npm run config` before starting a run; it is also checked automatically by ship, wf init and preflight.

shipConfig.$comment: A track is a weight of document. It is resolved from the document's path by `match`, or named with `--track`. Stage order is fixed: preflight, pre_implement, implement, static_gate, review, qa. Every track must list all six; a stage it does not run is `enabled: false` rather than absent, so a reader never has to know the full list to see what is missing. `static_gate` and `qa` may not be disabled on any track — a lighter document buys speed against the stages that read intent, never against the ones that check the result.

spec.$comment: A three-file spec bundle that the refine loop admitted. The full pipeline.

pre_implement.$comment: Compiles the spec into handoff.json. `strict` answers a closed compile checklist by id and writes shippingSurfaces; the `classic` variant is the original open prompt. Both write the same handoff.json.

implement.$comment: Writes the code. The default is one opus implementer, synchronous — the safe shape for a small or tangled diff. The `orchestrated` variant is an opus lead that splits the handoff into disjoint file sets and dispatches sonnet shards in parallel waves; it is faster and only sound when the plan's file globs are disjoint. Pick one for a run with --implement-profile.

review.$comment: Judges the diff. The default gives each shard open-ended judgement and no checklist, on opus. The `sweeps` variant gives it the enumerate-then-judge method in .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md, on sonnet. shardSize is the largest number of files one shard is handed. Pick one for a run with --review-profile.

solo.$comment: One reviewer, synchronous, over the whole slice. Same definition the children run; no lead, no split. The safe shape for a small diff, and the way to A/B a lead against the agent it dispatches.

convergence.$comment: Retry is the exception. Only a finding addressed to code, carrying a witness, and uncontested is ever retried.

timeoutMin.$comment: Fuses, not targets. A stage that runs past one understands nothing about why.

bug.$comment: An investigation report. It already carries the cause to file:line and the fix approach, so there is nothing left to compile into a plan.

pre_implement.$comment: No plan is compiled. The implement and review prompts name the report instead, and a review finding addressed to `handoff` routes to implement.

review.$comment: A defect fix earns the careful reviewer: the code around a bug is the code that already fooled somebody.

solo.$comment: One reviewer, synchronous, over the whole slice. Same definition the children run; no lead, no split. The safe shape for a small diff, and the way to A/B a lead against the agent it dispatches.

convergence.$comment: maxHandoffReplans is 0 because there is no plan stage to replan; a `handoff` finding is routed to implement instead.

patch.$comment: A change of agreed behaviour small enough to state and check in one file. Admission is the entry condition in .claude/skills/patch/SKILL.md, not a judged round.

pre_implement.$comment: No plan is compiled. The patch note is the plan; its file bound stands in for the handoff's globs.

implement.$comment: No orchestrated variant: the entry condition bounds a patch at two product files, and a lead that shards one file is pure overhead.

review.$comment: The cheap shape by default — a patch diff is small enough for one shard, and the checklist is what a small diff needs. The `open` variant buys the careful reviewer when a patch turns out to touch something load-bearing.

solo.$comment: One reviewer, synchronous, over the whole slice. Same definition the children run; no lead, no split. The safe shape for a small diff, and the way to A/B a lead against the agent it dispatches.

convergence.$comment: maxCodeAttempts is low on purpose. A patch that needs many attempts was misfiled — the run halting is the signal that it is a spec, and raising this number only hides that.

breakers.$comment: Whole-run fuses, the same for every track, enforced by scripts/ship.mjs before each stage is dispatched. runTokenCap counts every token the agents report - input, output and both cache figures - summed over the stage logs, so it survives a --resume. The observed range is 1.6M for a patch run and 155M for the largest spec run; the cap sits above that and catches a runaway, not a long run.

isolation.$comment: Worktrees isolate files and nothing else. Ports, both databases, the mail sink and .local-storage are shared, so runs are serialised until those are per-run too: concurrentRuns is the lock's invariant and the validator refuses any other value.

refine.$comment: The pre-pipeline gate, and the only thing here that is not per-track: it judges spec bundles, which is the one track that requires it. T0 is a script, T2 is the judge (full, then the previous repair's range), T1 is the pipeline's pre_implement run once after a clean verdict. Rounds are judged rounds; the loop also stops when a round does not shrink the blocker count, a finding survives a repair, or a repair adds more than maxGrowthPerFinding net lines to the bundle per blocker. A blocker filed under a rule outside blockingRules is demoted to a note.
refine.$profiles: profile picks who judges and who repairs. `solo` is a single opus judge, synchronous, one pass over the whole bundle. `sharded` is an opus judge that splits the criteria families across sonnet shards, then decides what is worth returning — faster and cheaper per pass, and the judge still signs every finding. Override for one run with --profile.
refine.$enforcement: requireCriteriaMap: a judged verdict carrying no criteria map is a judge error, retried, never recorded as a pass — by the register's own definition a criterion absent from the map was not run. requireJudgeModel: the model the SDK reports at init must be the one asked for; a substitution is recorded and the round is retried. shipRequiresRefine: `wf.mjs init` refuses a spec whose loop ledger is not a pass, or whose bundle changed after the round that judged it; it applies only to tracks with requiresRefine true, and `--accept-unrefined <reason>` overrides it and is recorded in run.json.

sharded.$note: One shard per member of the bundle, dispatched by the loop before the judge runs. The register's where column says which member answers each criterion; judge criteria never reach a shard.
